title: Implement backport labels + cherry-pick bot for Runtime LTS release branches
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
We need a consistent workflow for selecting, approving, and executing backports into the Runtime LTS branch (e.g., runtime-1.18-lts). This ticket covers:

1) Repo labels for backport selection + approval
2) Automation to open backport PRs (cherry-picks) against the LTS branch, track conflicts, and keep state visible to Release Eng + Runtime leads.

Motivation: LTS patch cadence + backport policy requires low-friction, low-risk cherry-picks with clear audit trails. Today, backports are ad-hoc and rely on manual cherry-pick + inconsistent metadata (hard to generate reliable release notes, hard for Support/SRE to understand what landed in a patch).

Scope
- Add and document labels:
  - backport-candidate (proposed for backport; not approved)
  - lts-approved (explicit approval for LTS inclusion)
  - lts-backport-conflict (automation detected conflicts)
  - release-notes/* taxonomy tags used by release-notes generator (consumed by ENG-4826)
- Add a bot/automation path that:
  - Can be triggered by labeling or a slash-command comment
  - Cherry-picks into runtime-1.18-lts (and optionally other release branches)
  - Opens a backport PR with standardized template (risk, test plan, perf notes, links)
  - Mirrors relevant labels from the source PR (e.g., release-notes/perf, release-notes/bugfix)
  - Handles conflicts by marking the backport PR and posting next steps

Non-goals
- Full multi-branch backport fanout (we only need runtime-1.18-lts for initial pilot)
- Auto-merge of backports (approval gates remain manual)
- Replacing Release Eng runbook (this is a helper; runbook remains source of truth)

Acceptance criteria
- Labels exist in the redwood/runtime repo and are used in at least one pilot backport end-to-end.
- Bot can create a backport PR from a source PR (happy path) and sets:
  - Correct base branch (runtime-1.18-lts)
  - Title format: "[LTS Backport] <original title> (#<original_pr>)"
  - Links back to original PR and includes cherry-pick provenance (commit SHAs)
  - Applies lts-backport + lts-approved (if the source PR has lts-approved) and release-notes/* labels
  - Assigns required reviewers (Runtime on-call + Release Eng) and sets CODEOWNERS-required checks
- Conflict path:
  - Bot detects cherry-pick conflict and either (a) opens PR in conflict state with clear instructions or (b) fails with actionable output.
  - Adds lts-backport-conflict label and posts a comment with git commands + suggested conflict owner (original author + Runtime stability)
- Auditability:
  - Backport PR body contains a "Backport metadata" section with original PR link, original merge commit, target branch, and bot run id.

Implementation notes
- Prefer GitHub Actions + a lightweight script (pr-merge commit lookup + git cherry-pick) over standing up a full Probot app for v1.
- Use a dedicated GitHub token with minimal permissions (scoped to repo) for PR creation.
- Triggers:
  - Label trigger: apply backport-candidate + add comment "Backport to: runtime-1.18-lts" OR apply lts-approved with a "backport-target/runtime-1.18-lts" label.
  - Comment trigger: /backport runtime-1.18-lts
- Edge cases:
  - PR merged via squash: use merge commit SHA from GitHub API; cherry-pick that commit.
  - PR has multiple commits: still cherry-pick merge commit (squash) or list of commits (merge) depending on merge method.
  - PR touches generated code: require explicit confirmation checkbox in template.

Links
- Epic: ENG-4821 Runtime LTS initiative
- Related PRs:
  - PR (labels): sources/github/redwood/pr-23201-add-backport-candidate-labels-and-release-notes-tags.json
  - PR (helper script): sources/github/redwood/pr-23222-cherry-pick-helper-script-for-lts-backports.json

Owners
- Devon Price (implementation)
- Connor O'Brien (workflow + Release Eng requirements)
- Samir Qureshi / Kira Volkov (runtime stability / conflict resolution feedback)

Open questions
- Do we require lts-approved to be present before bot runs, or allow bot run on backport-candidate (creating PR in Draft)? Proposed: bot can run on backport-candidate, but backport PR opens as Draft unless lts-approved exists.
- Reviewer set: should SRE be auto-requested for all backports or only those labeled security/Sev1? Proposed: SRE requested when labels include security or severity/sev1.
comments: 2025-01-29 (Connor O'Brien): Marking this P0 for pilot. We need labels + automation before we cut runtime-1.18-lts and attempt the first patch. Please keep the workflow simple; Release Eng will own the "approve" step via lts-approved + perf gate sign-off.

2025-01-31 (Devon Price): Drafted label set and proposed trigger matrix. I’d like to avoid a Probot app for v1; GitHub Actions + a script invoked via workflow_dispatch + issue_comment should cover it. Will sync with Sahana on token/permissions.

2025-02-03 (Sahana Iyer): CI-wise, we can provision a fine-grained PAT in 1Password and scope to repo actions: write for PR creation + labels. We should avoid exposing it to forks; workflow should run on issue_comment from members only. Please add guardrails.

2025-02-04 (Samir Qureshi): Strong preference for Draft backport PRs until lts-approved is present. We’ve already had cases where a "candidate" fix later failed perf gates. Draft makes it clear this isn’t landing by default.

2025-02-06 (Devon Price): Implemented /backport runtime-1.18-lts comment trigger (members only). Bot resolves original PR merge SHA (handles squash/merge) and runs a cherry-pick into a new branch backport/<pr>-runtime-1.18-lts. If conflicts, it pushes the branch and opens a PR labeled lts-backport-conflict with instructions. Next: label plumbing and template.

2025-02-10 (Connor O'Brien): Please ensure the backport PR template captures perf impact + required perf suite link. For LTS we need at least a pointer to perf-canary run or an explicit "N/A" justification.
2025-02-12 (Kira Volkov): Conflict path request: add suggested owner in the comment (original PR author + @runtime-stability). We’ve lost time on "who owns conflict" in past release branches.

2025-02-14 (Devon Price): Labels merged (backport-candidate, lts-approved, lts-backport-conflict, release-notes/*). Backport script PR merged as well. Added logic: if source PR has lts-approved, backport PR is opened as Ready; otherwise Draft. Also mirrors release-notes/* labels and adds lts-backport label. Pending: docs in CONTRIBUTING + short runbook snippet for Release Eng.

2025-02-18 (Connor O'Brien): Tested on a low-risk doc PR and on a small runtime fix. Happy path works. For conflicts, we get the label + comment with steps. One tweak: include bot run URL in PR body for auditability (useful during incidents).

2025-02-20 (Devon Price): Added bot run URL + commit provenance block (original PR, merge SHA, cherry-picked SHA list, target branch). Also added reviewer auto-request: Runtime kernels/scheduling codeowners always; SRE only when labels include security or severity/sev1. Marking ready to close once we backport the first real fix to runtime-1.18-lts.
2025-02-21 (Connor O'Brien): Confirmed used for KV cache compaction crash backport (Sev1). Backport PR created cleanly and included provenance + release-notes/bugfix. Closing.
